question: A floor is 12 m by 9 m. If tiles of 1.5 m × 1.5 m are used, how many tiles are needed?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Number of tiles along the length = 12 ÷ 1.5 = 8

Number of tiles along the breadth = 9 ÷ 1.5 = 6

Total number of tiles required = 8 × 6 = 48

**∴ The correct answer is 48 tiles.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the floor (L) = 12 m

Breadth of the floor (B) = 9 m

Side of one square tile (a) = 1.5 m

**Formula Used:**

Number of tiles = Total Area of floor ÷ Area of one tile

Number of tiles = (L × B) ÷ a²

 12 m 9 m 
• Tile: 1.5 m × 1.5 m 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Area of the floor = 12 × 9 = 108 m²

⇒ Area of one square tile = 1.5 × 1.5 = 2.25 m²

⇒ Number of tiles = 108 ÷ 2.25

⇒ Number of tiles = 10800 ÷ 225 = 48

**∴ The correct answer is 48 tiles.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Rectangle

The area of a rectangle is the product of its length and breadth: Area = L × B. Its perimeter is defined as 2 × (L + B).

Area of a Square

The area of a square is the square of its side length: Area = a². Its perimeter is defined as 4 × a.

Tiling Concept

When covering a larger flat area with smaller uniform regular shapes (like tiles), the total number required is always the total area divided by the area of one unit shape.
